# Quanby Sign - Global AI Agent Rules

## Project Overview

Quanby Sign is a secure document signing platform built with **Next.js 15**, **tRPC**, **Drizzle ORM**, **NextAuth**, and **Supabase**. It provides role-based access control, guided eSigning, approvals, and audit-ready history for stakeholders including individuals, businesses, legal teams, regulators, and admins.

## Technology Stack

- **Frontend**: Next.js 15 (App Router)
- **Backend**: tRPC for type-safe API calls
- **Database**: Drizzle ORM with type-safe database operations
- **Authentication**: NextAuth.js
- **Storage**: Supabase
- **Styling**: Shadcn UI component library
- **Package Manager**: pnpm (always use `pnpm` instead of npm/yarn)

## Critical Project Structure Rules

### Directory Organization

```
app/                  # ❌ ONLY Next.js reserved files (pages, layouts, routes)
├── (site)/           # ✅ Route groups and page.tsx files only
├── api/              # ✅ API routes only
└── globals.css       # ✅ Global styles only

features/             # ✅ ALL your business logic goes here
├── [feature-name]/
│   ├── api/          # ✅ tRPC routers, schemas, hooks
│   ├── components/   # ✅ Feature-specific UI components
│   ├── lib/          # ✅ Feature-specific utilities
│   ├── server/       # ✅ Server actions, DB operations
│   └── utils/        # ✅ Feature utilities

core/                 # ✅ Shared/reusable code
├── components/       # ✅ Shared UI components
├── context/          # ✅ React contexts
├── hooks/            # ✅ Shared React hooks
├── lib/              # ✅ Shared utilities
└── middleware/       # ✅ Shared middleware

services/             # ✅ External service integrations
├── email/            # ✅ Email service
├── next-auth/        # ✅ NextAuth setup
├── drizzle/          # ✅ Drizzle schema and migrations
├── supabase/         # ✅ Supabase client
└── trpc/             # ✅ tRPC setup
└── etc**/
```

### Business Logic Placement

- **ALL business logic** must go in `/features/[feature-name]/` folders
- Keep features isolated and self-contained
- Never put business logic in the `app/` directory

## File Naming Conventions

- **Components**: kebab-case (`user-profile.tsx`, `document-signer.tsx`)
- **Files**: kebab-case (`user-profile.utils.ts`, `auth-validation.schema.ts`)
- **Folders**: kebab-case (`user-management/`, `document-signing/`)
- **tRPC files**: `feature-name.router.ts`, `feature-name.schema.ts`, `feature-name.hooks.ts`

## Coding Standards

### TypeScript

- Use TypeScript everywhere - no `.js` files allowed
- Define proper types for all data structures
- Use tRPC for type-safe API communication

### Component Structure

- Use Shadcn UI components as the base component library
- Feature-specific components go in `/features/[feature-name]/components/`
- Shared components go in `/core/components/`
- Follow React best practices with hooks and functional components

### Database & API

- Use Drizzle ORM for all database operations
- Define schemas in `/services/drizzle/`
- Use tRPC routers in `/features/[feature-name]/api/`
- Server actions go in `/features/[feature-name]/server/`

### Authentication & Security

- Use NextAuth for authentication flows
- Implement role-based access control (RBAC)
- Secure sensitive operations with proper authorization checks

## Development Workflow

1. Use `pnpm` for all package management
2. Run `pnpm check` before committing
3. Update `.env.example` and `env.js` when adding environment variables
4. Keep features isolated in their own `/features/[name]/` folder

## Environment Setup

- Copy `.env.example` to `.env`
- Configure Supabase, email, and API keys
- Run `pnpm db:generate && pnpm db:push` for database setup
- Start development with `pnpm dev`

## Key Features to Consider

- Secure document access with role-based permissions
- Envelope and recipient management
- Guided eSigning workflow
- Approval and review processes
- Smart notifications system
- Identity verification (KYC) with OCR
- Audit-ready action logging
- Progress dashboards
- Account management

## Scripts

- `pnpm dev` - Start development server
- `pnpm build` - Build for production
- `pnpm db:push` - Push database schema changes
- `pnpm db:generate` - Generate database types
- `pnpm db:migrate` - Run database migrations
- `pnpm db:studio` - Open database GUI (if configured)
- `pnpm check` - Check code quality and lint

# Tailwind CSS Size Utility Guidelines

## Rule: Use `size-*` for Square Dimensions

**Guideline 1:** Use Tailwind's `size-*` utility classes instead of separate `w-*` and `h-*` when width and height are the same.

**Examples:**

- `size-4` instead of `w-4 h-4`
- `size-6` instead of `w-6 h-6`
- `size-8` instead of `w-8 h-8`
- `size-12` instead of `w-12 h-12`

**Guideline 2:** Only use separate `w-*` and `h-*` classes when the width and height values are different.

**Guideline 3:** This applies to all size values including responsive variants like `md:size-6`, `lg:size-8`, etc.
